newsitem.title: JAPAN: China soybean officials to visit Japan next week.
newsitem.headline: China soybean officials to visit Japan next week.

text.p: China will send a delegation from its soybean industry to Japan next week to discuss export contracts for the first half of calendar 1997, officials said on Thursday.

Officials from the Chinese grain agency Cereals Oils and Feedstuffs Import and Export Corp and Heilongjiang province, which grows most of China's soybeans, will arrive in Tokyo on October 23 and leave October 30, a Chinese grain official said.

"They'll exchange views with Japanese importers on soybean output and possibly sales contracts for the January-June period of next year," the Chinese grain official said. Chinese soybeans are mainly used for making miso, or bean paste, in Japan.
The delegation was originally scheduled to visit Japan last July, but delayed that because output figures for this year's harvest were not available yet, industry officials said.
On the back of falling domestic grain stocks and rising inflation, China has been trimming soybean exports to overseas customers since last year.

Japan imported 3,300,805 tonnes of soybeans in the first eight months of this year, Finance Ministry data showed. Of that, it bought 122,662 tonnes from China, down from 151,088 tonnes during the same period last year.
